raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With unified memory, every reader in an iteration shares one plan's page table, built by the first reader that asks. A CUDA-graph reader builds it in place in its static buffer as `into[:rows, :width]`. `width` is the pages the batch's host lengths need, usually far narrower than the buffer's `max_num_pages`, so with 2+ rows the table is a strided view. A later eager trtllm_mha read of the same plan asking for no more rows gets that view. XQA and fmha_v2 take a table's row length from its width and ignore its strides, so #42930 added an assert for this case, which "no known configuration produces":

```text
AssertionError: trtllm_mha reads its page tables as packed rows, but the plan's table is a strided view of a wider buffer
```

#46837 (DFlash draft CUDA graph under attention DP) produces it. The draft graph is keyed by the rank-local batch and the target verify by the DP-wide max. In a round where the draft replays but the verify overflows the captured graph and runs eager, the draft builds the table in place and the verify reads the strided view. Under skewed DP load (one heavy rank, 2+ requests on the others) the scheduler dies on the first decode rounds. On main alone the DFlash draft graph is off under DP, so this lands first and #46837 needs no workaround.

The fix belongs in the reader. The other table readers already handle a strided table: FA3 passes the row stride, the gather and CSR readers pass `row_stride`, and the MLA readers copy. Building packed tables in the plan instead would add a copy to nearly every graph replay on every backend.

## Modifications

- trtllm_mha's eager `init_forward_metadata` packs the full and sliding-window page tables with `.contiguous()` instead of asserting they are packed. `.contiguous()` returns a packed table as it is; decode graph capture and replay do not run this path.
- `test_unified_eager_table_must_be_packed`, which pinned the assert, becomes `test_unified_eager_packs_a_table_a_graph_reader_built`, run for the full and the sliding-window table. A captured reader builds that table in place first; the eager read must then give packed tables carrying exactly the ids the graph reader built.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/attention/test_trtllm_mha_graph_metadata.py` with CUDA hidden (the 149 tests that need CUDA skip):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| main + the new test | 2 failed (both cases hit the assert), 64 passed |
| this PR | 66 passed |
| this PR without the sliding-window `.contiguous()` | only the `swa` case fails |
| this PR without the full `.contiguous()` | only the `full` case fails |

On GPU, with #46837 and #47644 applied: Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 + Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2 (block 8), 4× GB300, TP4 / attention DP4 / EP4 FlashInfer MegaMoE, `trtllm_mha`, page 64, unified memory, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 4`. A client keeps 9 requests on DP0 and 2 on each other rank for 4 minutes. The verify's DP-wide bucket then overflows the captured graph while the light ranks' drafts replay. Same tree and node for both runs; only this change differs:

| | Result |
|---|---|
| without this change | the assert above on all three light ranks in the first decode rounds; 0/15 requests completed |
| this PR | 246/246 requests, no asserts, server alive |

With this change, diagnostic counters (not part of this PR) show about 1,800 draft-built strided tables per light rank, each read and packed by an eager verify. The tree was main at `1f834c19` plus the MegaMoE autotune fix from #46213, which this image needs at startup; `trtllm_mha_backend.py` and the plan code are the same as on this branch's base.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. The copy happens only when an eager trtllm_mha read finds a table a captured reader built (`bs × width` int32); every other read already gets a packed table.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed: no flag or behavior change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

     forward_batch = _eager_batch([127, 300], ForwardMode.DECODE)
     runner_ids.bind_own_plan(forward_batch)
+    captured = torch.zeros((8, backend.max_num_pages), dtype=torch.int32)

-    runner_ids.copy_page_table(forward_batch.iteration_ids, out=captured[:2])
-    with pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="packed rows"):
-        backend.init_forward_metadata(forward_batch)
+    metadata = backend.forward_metadata
+    for table, table_v2p in (
